title: Resting-state EEG in Starvation and Recovery in children and adolescents with Anorexia Nervosa
summary: The aim of the study is to investigate differences in brain activity among adolescents with anorexia, depending on whether they are severely underweight or have already regained weight. The study focuses in particular on which changes in the brain are caused by being underweight and reverse with weight gain, and which persist regardless of weight changes.  To this end, electrical brain activity is measured, and potential influences of the severity and nature of psychological symptoms and physical effects are also examined using questionnaires and data from treatment. Some participants will be assessed at two time points. A control group of healthy adolescents will also be included for comparison. The goal is to better understand the disorder and its course and to improve treatment in the long term.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age: 12;00 bis 17;11 years

Patients (AN – Starvation):
- Diagnosis of typical AN (F.50.00/F50.01) or atypical AN (F50.1; aAN) according to DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria (World Health Organization, 2016) and in inpatient or stepped-care treatment
- %EBW: AN < 85%; aAN 85%–95%
- low fT3
- Primary or secondary amenorrhea
- ChEDE-Q score ≥ 4

Patients (AN – WR):
- Currently diagnosed with anorexia nervosa according to DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria (F50.1; World Health Organization, 2016), in inpatient or stepped-care treatment
- %EBW: ≥ 90% or individually determined minimum weight
- normal fT3

Control group:
- No psychiatric diagnosis 
- Normal body weight (%EBW ≥ 85%)
- Written informed consent from legal guardians and from the participant
- Sufficient proficiency in German
Exclusion criteria:
- Current suicidality
- Intellectual disability
- Severe medical, neurological, or developmental disorders (including dermatological conditions of the scalp)
- Implanted electrical or metallic medical devices incompatible with EEG/MRI
- Patients with involuntary hospital treatment or restriction by legal or court order
